title: Broad Bean’s Genome Beats Human’s Size
description: Most people assume the broad bean has a tiny genome like other legumes. In fact, its diploid DNA stretches to 13 gigabases, dwarfing the human genome and ranking among the largest plant genomes.
narration: BROAD BEAN IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture the broad bean’s DNA as modest, like most legumes. In reality its diploid genome actually spans about 13 gigabases—far bigger than the human genome. Vicia faba’s diploid genome holds roughly 13 gigabases of DNA, largely from amplified retrotransposons and repeats. That dwarfs the human genome’s 3.2 gigabases, making it one of the largest diploid plant genomes, currently known among field crops. Its massive DNA makes the bean a genetic giant among plants.
